## Six conflicts on files nobody wrote

*2026-09-03 19:42:37 · ci · record*

**Every forward merge in the [#141](https://github.com/dmarx/luria/issues/141) stack conflicted on the decision index,
its tag pages and the devlog book, and the last one against `main` did
too.** Six times, the same three to five generated files, resolved the
same way each time: take either side, `luria index`, commit. The author
asked the right question — hadn't we solved this? — and the answer was
half. Sources never conflict ([ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md)). Views conflicted because the
generation job ([ADR-029](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md)) committed them onto every branch, so two branches
carried two correct copies of one generated file. Decided as [ADR-tmphzwg9](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-tmphzwg9.md):
views are committed on the default branch only; a pull request regenerates
in the working tree, lints the regenerated tree in the same job, and
commits nothing.

**Why the same job.** [ADR-029](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md)'s warning — a checking job that regenerates
and commits nothing compares the generator against itself — was aimed at
the default branch, where a committed view is the artifact. On a pull
request the branch does not carry the views by design, so staleness is not
a property it has, and the same-job shape is the only one that can lint a
tree nobody committed. The remedy text now says which shape is meant
where; the test that pinned the old wording pins the new one.

**What got simpler.** The pull-request job needs no write permission, no
fork-safe checkout expression, and no `needs:`/SHA handoff: the default
merge-commit checkout is the right tree to check, and it is checked as it
would land. The generate action gained one input, `commit`, and the push
path is untouched.

**What it does not fix.** Branches that already carry regenerated views —
the five in the stack — keep conflicting with each other until they merge.
The routine for those is now written in CONTRIBUTING rather than known.

**Fired on itself.** This pull request is the first to run the new shape:
its own views are regenerated on the runner and not committed here.
